title: Balanced Binary Tree
oneLinerQuestion: Determine if a binary tree is height-balanced (|leftH - rightH| <= 1 for all nodes).
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Balanced Binary Tree problem requires determining whether a given binary tree is height-balanced, meaning the depths of the two subtrees of every node never differ by more than 1. A naive top-down approach computes subtree heights repeatedly, resulting in an inefficient O(N^2) time complexity. By computing heights in a bottom-up post-order DFS traversal, we can determine the balance status while calculating node heights simultaneously. If an imbalance is detected at any subtree, we immediately return a sentinel value (-1) to short-circuit further checks and propagate the failure up the call stack.

- Step 1: Recursive Helper Definition — We define a helper function `checkHeight(node)` that returns the height of the subtree if it is balanced, or `-1` if it is unbalanced.

- Step 2: Base Case (Empty Subtree) — If `node === null`, an empty subtree is balanced and has a height of `0`, so we return `0`.

- Step 3: Left Subtree Bottom-Up Check — We recursively compute the left subtree height: `const leftHeight = checkHeight(node.left)`. If `leftHeight === -1`, an imbalance was already detected below, so we return `-1` immediately to short-circuit execution.

- Step 4: Right Subtree Bottom-Up Check — We recursively compute the right subtree height: `const rightHeight = checkHeight(node.right)`. If `rightHeight === -1`, we likewise return `-1` immediately.

- Step 5: Subtree Balance Evaluation — We evaluate the balance condition at the current node: `if (Math.abs(leftHeight - rightHeight) > 1) return -1`. If balanced, we return the true height of the current subtree: `return 1 + Math.max(leftHeight, rightHeight)`.

- Step 6: Root Execution & Final Verdict — We initiate `checkHeight(root)`. The binary tree is balanced if and only if the final returned value is not `-1` (i.e., `checkHeight(root) !== -1`).

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(N) where N is the total number of nodes, as each node is visited at most once during the single bottom-up traversal. Space Complexity: O(H) auxiliary space on the recursion call stack, where H is the height of the tree (O(log N) for balanced trees, O(N) for skewed trees).
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION isBalanced(root):
    FUNCTION checkHeight(node):
        IF node IS NULL THEN RETURN 0
        leftH = checkHeight(node.left)
        rightH = checkHeight(node.right)
        IF leftH == -1 OR rightH == -1 OR ABS(leftH - rightH) > 1 THEN RETURN -1
        RETURN 1 + MAX(leftH, rightH)
    END FUNCTION
    RETURN checkHeight(root) != -1
END FUNCTION
